ci: stop the linux dependency step hanging for the whole job timeout (#1054)

The release build's apt step had no interactive-prompt suppression, no lock
timeout and no step timeout, so it could block forever. It did: one run sat
in this step from 19:48 to 20:48 until timeout-minutes 60 killed the job,
and every downstream job was skipped with it.

Three separate ways it can block, each closed:

needrestart is apt-hooked on ubuntu-22.04 and prompts for which services to
restart. DEBIAN_FRONTEND does not suppress that one - needrestart reads its
own NEEDRESTART_MODE.

unattended-upgrades holds the dpkg lock and apt waits with no timeout by
default. It is meant to be disabled on hosted images and currently is not:
actions/runner-images#13271 is open, regressed in the 2025-10-23 images and
affects 22.04 and 24.04. DPkg::Lock::Timeout bounds the wait.

debconf can prompt independently, which DEBIAN_FRONTEND covers.

The step timeout is the backstop and matters most on its own: it turns
silently burning the hour and losing the release into failing in 15 with a
log that says which package it died on.

fix(ats): stop false date-context criticals, and route translation through the active provider (#1051)

* fix(ats): stop a bare present-tense word from faking a date context

is_open_ended matched PRESENT_MARKERS anywhere in a line, so ordinary
prose ("Reduced actual costs by 20% in 2023") read as an open-ended
span and, via factual::unsupported_date_issues' own direct scan of the
same word list, turned a truthful year into a Critical the moment the
source didn't literally spell it out (HIGH: user-facing, blocks ok,
drives the repair loop to rewrite correct content).

Require the marker to sit right after a year (PRESENT_MARKER_ADJACENT_RE)
instead of a bare word search, and route factual.rs's date-context
check through the same structural predicate mod.rs::labels_the_entry_below
already uses (JobEntry or a trailing_date_column) so the two surfaces
can't drift apart again.

Tightening is_open_ended costs bare-marker recognition with no year
anywhere in the fragment ("Present" alone) - accepted, matches the
non-answer DATE_ONLY_MARKERS already gives "Today" alone. It also
silently dropped source_is_ongoing's separator-free coverage
("2021 Present", no dash) - a shape export::parser::DATE_RE itself
accepts - so tenure.rs gets a dedicated SPAN_MARKER_NO_SEP_RE arm to
keep that reading generous rather than closing a truthful long tenure
at its start year (MEDIUM: was reachable, no prior test covered it).

* fix(export): link a bare lowercase domain on an allowlisted tld

A bare portfolio domain with no path (aijobhunter.app, iamsaeed.dev)
rendered as plain text while a GitHub project url one line below, which
happened to carry a /path, rendered as a clickable link. Add a second
bare-domain arm in split_urls gated on lowercase + an explicit TLD
allowlist shared with validate/content/factual.rs's URL_RE, so a
capitalised library name spelled with a dot (Socket.IO, Bun.sh,
Nuxt.dev) still stays plain text and an open-ended TLD class can never
link a node.js-shaped token to an invalid host.

* fix(ats): widen the link guard to the domain the renderer now hyperlinks

BARE_DOMAIN_NO_PATH_RE (model/rich.rs) turns a bare lowercase domain on an
allowlisted TLD into a real hyperlink, but factual.rs's URL_RE couldn't see
that same shape: its bare-host arm needs a known code host, its other
bare-domain arm needs a trailing path. A hallucinated project domain with no
path contributed to neither source_urls nor generated_urls, so
factual.altered_project_link never fired even though the export rendered it
as a real, clickable, seemingly-verified link.

Add a fifth URL_RE arm mirroring the renderer's exact rule (lowercase +
closed TLD allowlist, no path), scoped (?-i:...) against the rest of the
pattern so a capitalised stack-line library name (Socket.IO, Bun.sh,
Nuxt.dev) still stays unmatched. Also correct rich.rs's doc comment, which
claimed its TLD list mirrors URL_RE's bare-host arm when it actually mirrors
the domain+path arm; the real bare-host arm is CODE_HOSTS-gated with a
narrower TLD set.

* fix(ai): translate through the active provider, not the embedding one

Translation read the persisted embedding config as a stand-in for the
active AI provider, so a claude-code user could have a job ad routed to
whatever Ollama chat model embeddings happened to be configured for (an
arbitrary /api/tags-first pick), taking 117s and starving concurrent
embed calls. It now reads ai_config::AiConfigStore::active_config and
always uses the user's own active model, never a pick; the cloud-provider
cost gate is unchanged. Also distinguishes a real Ollama transport timeout
from a connection refusal (both used to read "unreachable") across every
call site in ollama.rs, and logs the embedding model (not just the
provider) on both success and failure, including when the config read
itself falls back to a default.

Embedding routing through the active provider is a separate, out-of-scope
design decision (Claude Code has no embeddings API).

* feat(settings): add prompt quality control to the ai settings page

Canonical home for the global promptQuality preference, previously
changeable only from StepFineTune and AnalyzeLeftPanel — the tailor
pipeline had no control at all. Reads/writes the same store field, so
all three surfaces stay in sync. resolveEffectiveTier ignores the
preference for anything but a local Ollama provider, so the control
stays enabled but names the active provider and states the setting
does not apply to it whenever it is not Ollama.

* fix(export): revert the unsafe bare-domain-without-path link widening

urls_in() (validator, detect-a-link) and the stack filter in
pipeline/resume/source.rs (delete-if-a-link) are opposite consumers of the
same match set. The lowercase-bare-domain arm added to both split_urls
(model::rich) and URL_RE (validate::content::factual) to keep them in
lockstep had no email-aware branch, so it matched the domain half of an
ordinary email address as a bare "URL" (urls_in("jane@gmail.com") ->
["gmail.com"]), and on a title/description line - which carries no
names_a_resource filter - a lowercase library mention in ordinary prose
(bun.sh, vite.dev, socket.io) reopened the exact false-Critical shape this
file exists to prevent. A context-aware fix (only link a bare domain in a
contact/title-line context, never in free prose) would need to thread line
context through every split_urls call site across the renderer, which is
out of scope for this fix; reverting both arms is the safe option.

Add a shared-corpus parity test pinning that the renderer and validator
agree on link-shaped text, plus a dedicated regression test asserting
neither surface turns an email address into a phantom bare-domain link.

* fix(ats): stop deleting a resource-free stack token from the source resume

pipeline/resume/source.rs's stack-line filter dropped an item whenever
urls_in() found any match, with no names_a_resource guard - unlike its two
siblings in the same function (the labeled-span and bare-URL link capture),
which both skip a stack-line match that doesn't name a resource. A
technology token that merely looks host-shaped therefore got silently
deleted from the candidate's own stack line instead of kept as the
technology it is. Add the same names_a_resource guard the siblings use.

* fix(ats): remove a dead disjunct and its now-inverted doc comments

looks_like_date_span's `|| is_open_ended(s)` disjunct went dead when is_open_ended was changed to require a year before any of its own branches run:
is_open_ended can no longer be true while years_in(s) is empty, and years_in(s) being non-empty already makes looks_like_date_span true on its own,
so the OR can never change the result. Simplify to years_in(s) alone, and correct the two doc comments (on looks_like_date_span itself and on
is_date_column_segment) that still described the old bare-marker-with-no-year behaviour as current. is_date_column_segment is now identical to
looks_like_date_span, so delegate to it instead of duplicating the check.

* test(ats): cover the stack-line names_a_resource guard directly

seed_one_project's stack-line filter had no direct test - the data-loss bug it fixes (any urls_in match dropping the item, with
no names_a_resource guard) went unnoticed because the reverted arm-5 widening was the only common way to trigger it, and
reverting that widening also happened to stop reproducing the bug. crates.io still reproduces it today: it is a code-host
arm-3 match that names no resource. Pin it end to end through seed_projects.

* fix(egress): repair the log-leak allowlist and add content-anchored matching

An unrelated 23-line insertion shifted a declared documents/mod.rs log site
from line 1153 to 1176, breaking check-log-error-leaks.mjs both ways
(undeclared at the new line, stale at the old one) and blocking the push.
Beyond the line fix, ALLOWLIST entries can now opt into a `sig` (the call's
own format-string literal) so an entry survives the NEXT line shift as long
as it stays the only declared entry with that (file, sig) pair in an
unambiguous match; two genuinely duplicated messages still each need their
own declaration.

* fix(ai): restore a fast reachability gate before translation attempts

Two regressions in the active-provider translation routing fix: `state`
panics if AiConfigStore isn't managed yet, where `try_state` degraded
gracefully per this function's own "never an error" contract, and dropping
`reachable_chat_model`'s 3s Ollama health probe (in favor of the pure
validate_model check) means an unreachable or busy local daemon now eats the
full completion deadline (minutes, scaled by effort) per translation
attempt instead of a fast skip -- the same run-starving shape this fix's own
commit was written to close. Restores try_state and a should_attempt_translation
gate that gives Ollama alone a cheap reachability check before the call; CLI
agents (newly reachable by this fix, intentionally) have no analogous cheap
probe and proceed regardless.

* fix(ai): sanitize two new tracing:: log sites and split embedding out of documents

documents/mod.rs sat at exactly R8's 1400-LOC hard cap with zero headroom,
bought partly by trimming comments; the next one-line change would fail the
architecture test. Extracts the self-contained embedding round-trip +
posting-vector cache resolver into documents/embedding.rs (re-exported flat
at documents:: so every existing crate::documents::X call site is
unaffected), leaving 185 lines of real headroom.

Also sanitizes two tracing::warn! sites this branch introduced in the same
area (embedding_config's rusqlite::Error read failure, and embed()'s
provider-call failure) -- check-log-error-leaks.mjs only scans log:: macros,
so tracing:: is a blind spot the guard can't see; one of the two wraps a raw
reqwest::Error, and Gemini authenticates via a `?key=` query param.

* fix(ats): stop a non-dash separator from closing an ongoing role

74b95c9f replaced is_open_ended's bare-marker branch with an adjacency
regex whose separator class is [-/] | to | bis | until | hasta | au | a |
tot | fino | ate. A pipe, middot, comma or parenthesis is not in it, and
two callers relied on the old looseness.

tenure.rs::source_is_ongoing answered the one direction its own doc calls
dangerous: "... | 2015 | Present" read as CLOSED, career_span_years
collapsed from 11 to 0, supported_years fell from 13 to 2, and a truthful
"11 years of experience" raised a false factual.inflated_experience
Critical (CRITICAL: user-facing, blocks ok, drives the repair loop to
rewrite correct content). SPAN_MARKER_NO_SEP_RE covered only the
whitespace-only spelling, so it missed every other separator.

Replace it with names_a_present_marker: the marker anywhere on a line the
caller has already established carries a year. No separator list at all -
export::parser::DATE_RE, this codebase's own definition of a job entry's
date range, allows 30 arbitrary characters there, so any enumeration
fails the same way one spelling further out.

Same root cause, second caller: is_date_only reached a separator-free
date column ("..., 2015 Present") only through is_open_ended, so that
column stopped opening a role. Bullets rejoined the entry above, employer
salvage never ran, and unsupported_date_issues - routed through
trailing_date_column by 74b95c9f - went silent on those lines (HIGH, five
consumers). Read PRESENT_MARKERS as a TOKEN there, exactly the way
DATE_ONLY_MARKERS beside it always was; the date_words gate has already
rejected prose, so the restriction protecting is_open_ended is not needed
here. The lists stay disjoint - this reads both, it does not merge them.

The prose leak stays fixed and is re-asserted explicitly: is_open_ended
is unchanged, and the three reported sentences are pinned false.

* fix(egress): require entry-side uniqueness before a sig satisfies an allowlist entry

Content-anchored (sig) matching required exactly one DETECTED LEAK but not
exactly one DECLARED ENTRY, so N allowlist entries sharing a (file, sig) were
all satisfied by the same single leak and the N-1 stale ones were never
reported. A sig could also be satisfied by a leak a DIFFERENT entry already
declares line-exactly, leaving the sig entry with no site of its own and still
counted as live.

Both directions can only ever suppress a stale-entry error, never an
undeclared-leak one: a second site with the same message makes the leak bucket
length 2, which disables sig matching for that bucket outright. Latent today
(one entry uses sig) and live the moment the header's planned mass-sig
migration lands, since duplicated message text is exactly what produces
duplicate sigs.

Entries are now bucketed by (file, sig) the same way leaks are, and a pairing
counts only when both buckets hold exactly one item and the leak is not already
declared by line. Three regression tests cover the two-entry, five-entry and
already-claimed-leak shapes; the existing ambiguous-leak and wrong-file cases
stay as controls. All three fail against the previous implementation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(settings): assert the ollama-only note exactly so it survives no mutant

The `/settings\.promptQuality\.ollamaOnlyNote/` regex is a prefix match, so it
passed against a component whose key was typo'd to `ollamaOnlyNoteX` AND
against one that dropped the `{ provider }` interpolation entirely — both
mutants measured, both survived. Asserting the exact rendered text, which the
`t` mock builds as `<key> <param values>`, pins the key and the interpolation
together; both mutants now fail.

The negative assertion in the sibling test keeps its regex: a broader matcher
is the stronger form when proving absence.

ci: group dependabot updates by area, and unblock local pushes (#1050)

* ci: group dependabot updates by the part of the app they touch

Cargo and github-actions only grouped typst and codeql-action, so every
other bump opened its own PR: 5 Rust crates and 4 workflow actions at once.
npm already had a catch-all and collapsed to a single PR.

Adds the same catch-all to both, named for the area so the PR title says
which part of the app moved (desktop-rust, ci-actions), and renames npm's
group to javascript for the same reason. Majors stay individual on all
three, unchanged.

Both catch-alls carry exclude-patterns for the existing lockstep groups.
exclude-patterns beats patterns, so typst and codeql-action stay in their
own PRs regardless of group order in this file - a partial bump inside a
large catch-all PR would not be visible.

npm stays one entry: workspace members share the root pnpm-lock.yaml and
cannot be split per-directory.

* test: move the vitest browser server off a windows-reserved port

Vitest hardcodes defaultBrowserPort = 63315 and allocates upward from
there. Windows reserves blocks for Hyper-V/WSL in that neighbourhood
(63285-63384 here), and a reserved port is still offered by the resolver
but refused at bind, so every push died on:

  Error: listen EACCES: permission denied ::1:63315

with all 6956 tests passing - vitest counts the unhandled error as a
failure. Reproduced identically three times, sandboxed and not.

Pins browser.api.port to 6317, below the dynamic port range where these
exclusions live. The default was already a fixed port, so this is not
trading a dynamic allocation for a static one - it is the same shape at
an address the OS will actually hand over.

Verified: vitest run --project storybook now serves on localhost:6317,
46 files / 180 tests, exit 0.

fix: stop a false language critical and read today as a date column (#1038)

* fix(documents): recognise today/actualidad/oggi/aujourd'hui as date columns

is_date_only used exact-token equality against PRESENT_MARKERS, which never
carried English "Today" or its Spanish/French/Italian equivalents, so an
entry line ending in one of those spellings failed to open its own role and
had its header and bullets absorbed into the entry above it.

Added a separate DATE_ONLY_MARKERS list consumed only by is_date_only rather
than extending the shared PRESENT_MARKERS: that list is also matched by
is_open_ended and validate::content::factual via single-word, no-structure-
required matching, and "today" is common enough English prose vocabulary
that adding it there would risk turning ordinary bullets into false date
contexts (confirmed the same failure mode already live for "actual").
is_date_only requires every token on the line to be a digit, month or
marker, so exact-token equality against a whole date column is safe by
construction regardless of what the list holds.

* fix(documents): widen date-only markers to the currently/presente family

DATE_ONLY_MARKERS only covered the "today" spelling family, so English
"Currently" and the Iberian/Italian "Presente" spelling — both ordinary
CV date-column endings, and Presente reachable via the es/pt/br locale
profiles shipped in #1009 — still failed to open their own role.

Extended the list with the "currently" family (currently, presente,
hoje, atualmente, hoy, actuellement, attualmente, derzeit, vandaag),
kept as literal spellings rather than a shared stem: this const is
already read by a whole-line gate, and nothing stops a future caller
reading it against free text the way PRESENT_MARKERS is, so a prefix
rule would reintroduce the exact hazard the list is separate to avoid.
"nu" (Dutch/Swedish "now") is deliberately left out and documented —
two letters collides far more readily than the rest of the list, and
"heden" already covers the Dutch case.

Measured the tenure.rs path for the same gap (2020 - Atualmente):
career_span_years still reads it as ongoing, because source_is_ongoing
is structural (year + separator + non-year tail) rather than
vocabulary-driven, so no second defect exists there.

* fix(validate): require function-word evidence before a language critical

whatlang's confidence() is a top-1-vs-top-2 margin, not a correctness
probability: a noun-phrase-heavy block (an ordinary skills line, a terse
CV) starves its n-gram model of the closed-class function words it needs
to read a language from at all, so it can land on the wrong Latin-script
language with maximum confidence and is_reliable() == true.

is_language_mismatch now also requires collision-pruned, distinctive
function-word evidence of some other curated language before a confident
Latin-script read becomes an accusation. Non-Latin scripts are unaffected
- whatlang already reads those reliably regardless of function-word
density. The per-section pass now routes through the same function
instead of a duplicated check, closing the same gap at both scopes.

* fix(documents): add spanish actualmente, harden the date-marker tests

Spanish resumes writing an open-ended column as "Actualmente" (one
letter off Portuguese "atualmente", already present) reproduced the
original defect: the header and bullets absorbed into the entry above.
Added the missing spelling and recorded the multi-word-column boundary
(en la actualidad, en cours, ad oggi, bis heute, etc.) as a known,
deliberate limitation rather than a silent gap.

Test hardening from review:

- table test now collects every failing spelling instead of asserting
  inside the loop, so a future dropped/typo'd marker is reported by
  name instead of being hidden behind the first failure
- dropped the paired "prose" loop: every row only passed because the
  tokenizer gate rejects ordinary sentences before any marker is
  consulted, so it proved nothing about DATE_ONLY_MARKERS specifically
  and duplicated a_date_column_needs_more_than_a_year_in_it under a
  misleading name
- added a one-line disjointness assertion so DATE_ONLY_MARKERS and
  PRESENT_MARKERS never silently start sharing a spelling, which is
  the entire safety argument for keeping the two lists separate

Documented a second safety property the review surfaced: since no
DATE_ONLY_MARKERS entry is ever added to PRESENT_MARKERS, a line built
entirely from digits/months/DATE_ONLY_MARKERS tokens still can't pass
is_date_only without a real year or a genuine PRESENT_MARKERS marker,
because looks_like_date_span never consults the new list.

* fix(validate): redesign language evidence as pairwise, not a global pool

Three review findings, all confirmed by measurement:

- a single function-word pool pruned across all seven curated languages
  left Spanish (30 survivors) and Portuguese (33) too thin to evidence
  themselves, so a genuinely Spanish/Portuguese document against another
  target silently stopped raising a real Critical. Evidence is now
  pairwise per comparison (found vs target), not globally pruned.
- short tokens (ci, vi, io, ha, da, ti, os, em, am, im, zu, el, na, ai,
  et, au) collide with common English abbreviations/TLD fragments in
  free text; closed with a named denylist plus curating "per" into the
  English list, rather than a blanket length floor (which was tried
  first and measured to also exclude Italian's own short core
  vocabulary, briefly regressing a true positive).
- the section-scoped pass had its own untested detected_language
  comparison; it now routes through the same is_language_mismatch the
  document pass uses.

Adds a comparative margin (found's evidence must exceed target's own in
the same text) and a title-case-sandwich exclusion (a connector wedged
between two Capitalised words is almost always part of a proper noun's
own official name) to separate "an English document naming a foreign
institution" from a genuine mismatch, without reopening the Spanish
regression. Also fixes the tr/vi corroboration gate to key off Latin
script rather than curated-vocabulary membership, closing a
zero-evidence Critical hole.

* fix(validate): dedupe the portuguese word list, add a duplicate guard

A wider sweep for the zijn-in-NL class of bug found a second instance:
"a" and "se" each listed twice in FUNCTION_WORDS_PT. Harmless under the
current HashSet-based evidence count, but a silent authoring mistake.
Adds a permanent test asserting no curated list has an internal
duplicate, so a third one fails loudly instead of by inspection.

* fix(validate): remove two unproven language-evidence suppressors

Delete AMBIGUOUS_SHORT_TOKENS and distinctive_evidence_confirms's
comparative margin after measuring, for each, that no realistic
document needs it: disabling either left every validate::content
behavioural test green, and only the mechanism's own manufactured unit
test went red. The denylist's one measured trigger required an
adversarial string of disconnected foreign idioms with no connecting
English grammar, a shape this validator's real input never produces,
at a real cost - it permanently denied el/zu/na/et/di/ci, high-
frequency function words of the exact languages the pairwise fix was
written to protect. Removed on the strength of measurement, not kept
on the strength of the argument for them, per this module's own
history.

Replaces the deleted unit tests with ones for the mechanisms that
remain (the single-letter floor, the absolute evidence floor) and
records the measurement in the module doc so a future edit does not
re-add either suppressor without re-measuring.

* fix(validate): replace the title-case sandwich with a measured floor

The title-case-sandwich exclusion in pairwise_evidence_count deleted
German's evidence wholesale: standard German CV register is nominal
("Aufbau und Betrieb der Zahlungsplattform"), German capitalises every

fix(landing): serve the /world clips from r2, which can send cors headers (#1032)

PR #1031 moved the clips to a GitHub release and broke the route. The release
URLs resolve fine to curl, which is how the check passed and why the break

* feat(validate): catch invented tenure, certifications and education

Three invention classes the metric family cannot see, wired in with the tiers
the calibration commit measured rather than the tiers their names suggest.

factual.inflated_experience (Critical). Compares the NUMBER in "8+ years of
experience" against what the source states in words and against the span its
own employment dates cover, plus one year of slack for the months a year column
does not carry. Only an OVERSTATEMENT fires: rounding down is not a fabrication,
so the rule is "must not exceed", never "must appear". Comparing numbers is what
makes this survive a German résumé generated from an English source, which is
the path #1004 shipped.

factual.unsourced_certification (Critical). A curated issuer list plus a curated
acronym list, never "looks capitalised". A certification word with no issuer
near it is not a credential, so "certified the release each Thursday" reports
nothing. CSM and CPA are left out of the acronym list by name: both are real
certifications and neither is unambiguous.

factual.unsourced_institution (Warning, absence only). A2c was specified as a
value comparison on the institution name. Measured, it produced a false finding
on truthful cross-language output: "Technische Universität München" is the
correct German rendering of an English source's "Technical University of
Munich" and shares no token with it. City names translate exactly as degree
titles do. What ships instead is the translation-safe residue — the generated
document names a place of study while the source names none at all — and it
stays advisory even there. The rejected comparison is still executed by
institution_value_comparison_fires_on_a_correctly_translated_institution, so
the rejection keeps being true rather than being a comment.

The tenure check reads the clock once, to close an open-ended "2019 - Present",
and validates it: a clock reading earlier than a year the documents name is
discarded along with the span evidence instead of shrinking the allowance into
an accusation.

Both Criticals join report::FABRICATION_CODES because a Critical that is not
listed there keeps its run in needsReview forever, and neither has a section the
repair loop could regenerate - SectionKey has no Certifications variant.

The ACRONYM arm matches an uppercase, word-bounded token from a curated

language, and three review rounds produced no false positive from it. It stays
Critical.

The ISSUER arm reads unbounded natural language in seven languages,
discriminating with adjacency plus three curated vocabularies. It shipped "4 of

measured" and broke on the next pass again. That is the evidence class the
tenure check already ships as a Warning, with the same cadence, so it becomes
factual.unsourced_credential at Warning severity. Two codes rather than one,
because `issue` reads severity from the code table — which is what makes the
Critical unreachable from the prose path.

The clause-shape rule read sentences about SYSTEMS as claims about people,
fifteen times out of fifteen: "Rebuilt a platform with 15 years of accumulated
technical debt", "Joined a team with 12 years of shipping history", and the same

subject must name a person or be absent. Two tokens of it are read, because a
job title is routinely two words and the head noun comes last in some languages
and first in others. The follower list is deliberately not where this is fixed:
of, in, on and at follow any counted noun phrase whatever.

The role-noun rule did not fix the vendor terms. `engineer` matched as a

* feat(match): report hard constraints beside the score instead of blending them into it

Track E1 of the architecture audit.

`combined = f(semantic, ats)` measures how much of a posting's vocabulary the
résumé carries. It is a good relevance number and it structurally cannot answer
"could I actually take this job?", so a candidate who fails a non-negotiable
still scores well on keyword overlap. The fix is not to fold a penalty into the
number — it is to answer the second question separately.

`match_resume` now returns a `constraints.checks` field beside the score. Three
rules hold it up:

* it never touches the score. The verdict is computed in the L3 command AFTER
  the kernel returns, so it is not an input to `score_one` and never enters the
  `match_scores` cache — whose key is composed of SCORING inputs only, and would
  therefore have served a stale verdict for a whole TTL the moment the user
  edited their preferences. Out here, a cache HIT still gets a fresh verdict,
  and the Autopilot and extension entry points that share the kernel are
  byte-identical;
* it never hides a job. Nothing filters, sorts or gates on it. A wrong knock-out
  tells the user not to bother applying, which costs far more than a wrong
  percentage;
* absence of evidence is never evidence. `ConstraintStatus` has FOUR values, and
  the two "we don't know" ones are distinct from both a pass and a fail:
  `unknown` (the candidate stated a preference, the posting says nothing, or
  what they stated is not comparable) and `noPreference` (the candidate has
  expressed nothing at all — differently actionable, since the user can fix that
  one). A `notMet` requires positive evidence on BOTH sides, and each check
  carries each side's own words so that is a checkable property of the payload
  rather than a promise. It is enforced inside the one constructor every check
  goes through, not as a post-pass a later constraint could skip.

ONE constraint ships, because one is what the app has honest candidate-side data
for. `location`: the user's stored job-search location (and its geocode-picked
country code) against the posting's location text and its board remote flag.
Both sides are real, persisted, user-entered data.

The audit's other three are refused, and the module says so in full:

* work authorization, ranked first, has NO candidate-side field anywhere — not
  on the contact profile, not in job preferences. The tempting proxy, the
  candidate's own address, is exactly the false accusation this repo already has
  a live incident from: living in one country is not evidence of lacking
  authorization in another;
* employment type has no persisted preference. `AutopilotTarget::work_type` is a
  per-autopilot SEARCH filter, and a work arrangement rather than an employment
  type;
* salary floor: `salary_expectation` is free text ("80k DOE") documented as an
  application ANSWER, not a stated floor, with no currency and no period, and
  the posting side is a structured range on one board. Comparing them needs a
  money parser plus an FX assumption — two invented facts per verdict.

The comparison itself reuses the scrape-time location matcher rather than
forking one. `location_filter` grows a three-valued `location_verdict`, and the
existing binary `location_mismatch` is redefined as exactly its `Mismatch`
projection — same behaviour, one home for the remote-marker list, the diaeresis
folding and the curated exonym table. `languages_align` does not apply: nothing
here reads the résumé or the JD body, stems a token or extracts a keyword.

Mutation-checked, ten ways. Two survived the first round and both were real
holes, now closed: the two-sided-evidence guard was a post-pass its test called
directly, so deleting it from `evaluate` stayed green — it is a constructor now;
and deleting the one line that wires the pass into the command left the whole
suite green, because a `#[tauri::command]` cannot be called from a test in this
crate, so a compile-time source scan pins it. The other eight — rendering
unknown as a pass, dropping the no-preference branch, deleting either remote
feature, dropping the posting-side evidence, making the scrape filter drop on
undecided, folding the verdict into `combined`, removing the evidence byte cap —
each fail by name.

The first cut published `notMet` for location. Two independent facts say it
must not:

  statement. `job_preferences.location` is written by one free-text "Preferred

  recommendations". `JobsPage` seeds its scrape form from it ONE WAY and never
  writes back, so a user who deliberately searches Austin while Settings still
  says Berlin leaves no trace. `PostingsCache` keeps postings from every past
  search and retains no per-posting `LocationSpec`, so this pass cannot even
  recover which search a posting came from — the honest sentence would have been
  "a setting you last touched months ago says Berlin", against every cached row;
* a failed substring match is absence of evidence, not evidence of conflict.
  `Mismatch` fires on `Germany`/`Berlin` (granularity), `Vienna`/`Wien` and
  `NYC`/`New York` (exonym and abbreviation outside the curated table),
  `Berlin`/`EMEA` and `Berlin`/`Multiple locations` (not place names), and
  `Berlin`/`Telecommute` (a remote synonym the marker list lacks). It would also
  fire across most of the primary aggregator: Adzuna never writes
  `extra.remote` — only the three remote-only boards do — so remote detection
  there rests entirely on location text Adzuna's `display_name` never carries.

The module's own rule 3 convicted it: two non-empty strings satisfied the
constructor's floor while not being evidence of a CONTRADICTION.

directions and never accuses. The three-valued matcher still earns its keep —
without it `Met` could not be told apart from "the posting states no location".

The severity distinction is the lesson, and it is recorded in the module: the
identical predicate is safe as a scrape-time post-filter, judging a posting
against a location the user typed seconds earlier and costing one row in one
search, and unsafe as a published verdict against every cached posting keyed off
a settings field. Reuse the matcher; re-derive the epistemics.

* fix(match): require a whole-token place match before claiming a location fits

The four-state contract's one confident state was still loose. `met` is a
positive claim rendered to the user — "this posting matches where you're
looking" — and it rested on the scrape filter's substring, any-token reading, so
a `San Francisco` preference agreed with a `San Diego` posting on the shared
`san`. Erring toward agreement rather than accusation makes that cheap, not
correct. A contract whose only confident state is loose has moved the
imprecision, not removed it.

The strictness lives in the epistemics layer, not in the shared matcher: the
scrape filter's conservatism is right where it is, because there the expensive
mistake is discarding a job.

So the matcher now reports WHAT it found and the constraint pass decides what is
claimable. `LocationVerdict::Match` splits three ways:

* `Remote` — the board flagged it or its location text carries a marker, so no
  place comparison applies;
* `PlaceMatch` — every token the user actually typed appears as a WHOLE token of
  the posting's location;
* `PlaceOverlap` — something matched, but only as a substring or on part of a
  multi-token request.

`location_mismatch` is still exactly the `Mismatch` projection, so the scrape
filter is byte-for-byte unchanged: `PlaceOverlap` keeps, as it always did. The
constraint pass maps `Remote | PlaceMatch` to `met` and everything else,
`PlaceOverlap` included, to `unknown`.

Exonyms are expanded PER TOKEN in the strict matcher rather than over the whole
needle list. Expansion adds a word the user never wrote — a "Munich" request
gains "münchen" — so requiring every needle in the expanded list to match would
fail the exact pair the curated table exists to bridge.

The cost is deliberate and one-directional: a request MORE specific than the
posting ("Berlin, Germany" against a bare "Berlin") now reads `unknown` rather
than `met`. That loses a true positive and never states a false one, and
`unknown` claims nothing.

Tests: a dedicated overlap case (San Diego, Santa Monica, Newark, and the
more-specific request) with a same-preference control that still reads `met`, so
this is a strictness rule and not a blanket refusal to match a two-token place.
The 140-cell distribution grows to 176 (11 places × 8 preferences × 2 flags) to
carry the San Francisco / San Diego pairing, and its hand-derived counts — 44
noPreference, 75 met, 57 unknown, 0 notMet — are what fail if the strict rule is
relaxed: that one cell moves from unknown to met.

Mutation-checked 19 ways, all caught. New this round: publishing `met` for an
overlap, grading every hit as a whole-token match, requiring only SOME requested
token instead of every one, dropping the per-token exonym expansion, degrading
the whole-token test to a substring test, and making the scrape filter drop on
an overlap.

* fix(match): bound the met claim to the setting it reads, and pin what it rests on

Five review findings. The first is the one that mattered: the epistemics were
re-derived in ONE direction only.

Every fact used to kill `notMet` is direction-neutral — `job_preferences.location`
is a search-personalization setting, `JobsPage` seeds from it one-way, and
`PostingsCache` keeps postings from every past search with no record of which
`LocationSpec` produced them. So the mirror case was equally false: the same
stale `Berlin` setting, against `Berlin` rows left over from an earlier search,
reported `met` — and if that rendered as "this posting matches where you're
looking" it was wrong for the same reason, from the same field.

Deleting `met` is not the answer; it would leave a contract with no positive
state and make the pass vacuous. The asymmetry is real and it is in what each
status ASSERTS:

* `notMet` asserted a CONFLICT — that the posting is somewhere the candidate will
  not go. Nothing establishes that relation, and no phrasing repairs it, because
  the fact was never in hand;
* `met` asserts a MATCH between two strings held in full. The relation — every
  token of the stored preference present in the posting's location — is
  established deterministically and stays true whichever search produced the row.

So `met` is repaired by bounding what it is a claim ABOUT. It says "your stored
Preferred Location matches this posting", never "matches where you're looking".
Fixed where the meaning is defined, since there is no renderer yet to correct
later: the check's wire id is now `preferredLocation` rather than `location` —
the id is what a renderer keys i18n off, so it is what stops the stronger
sentence being written by accident, and it leaves `location` free for a real
mobility constraint if candidate-side data ever exists. Also stated on the
variant, the module doc, and the three shared TS docs a UI author reads.

Also fixed:

* `met` for the shipped UI defaults silently depended on `MIN_TOKEN_LEN`. "San
  Francisco, CA", "New York, NY" and "London, UK" all read as matches ONLY
  because 3 drops the two-letter qualifier, while that constant's doc justified
  3 purely as scrape-filter noise control. Lowering it to 2 for a scrape-side
  reason flipped all three to `unknown` with nothing failing. Now pinned by
  test, and the constant records that it has a second consumer with a different
  risk posture;
* the verdict and the evidence were computed from different bytes — the
  unclamped location was compared, the clamped one reported — so a >200-byte
  location could match on a token outside its own evidence. Both sides are
  clamped once, before the comparison. The test is a replay: re-running the
  evaluation on exactly what the check REPORTS must reproduce what it decided;
* `checks_for_job` took the `PostingsCache` lock and re-scanned for a job id
  `job_text_for` had just scanned for. Since the verdict is deliberately
  recomputed on a `match_scores` cache HIT, that duplicate ran on every
  Jobs-page call — the path where the score costs nothing. The posting is
  resolved once and handed over; the pure half is split out so the hand-off is
  testable;
* `PlaceOverlap` named two situations of opposite evidential strength: a
  coincidental substring ("San Francisco"/"San Diego" on `san`) and a genuine
  whole-token hit with one unmatched qualifier ("Berlin, Germany"/"Berlin").
  Renamed `PlaceIncomplete` — named for the incompleteness both share rather
  than a strength neither guarantees — with both readings documented. Not split:
  nothing needs to tell them apart, and inventing a distinction ahead of a
  consumer is what was refused for salary and employment type.

fix(autopilot): jitter scheduled runs so default installs stop herding (#1018)

Track B3 of the architecture audit.

Schedules are clock-anchored, the tick is 60 s wide, and every record created
before the run-time picker defaults to 09:00. So every default-schedule install
in a time zone hits the same third-party APIs inside the same minute. This is
not theoretical here: the desktop log already shows scheduled runs failing with
`adzuna: HTTP 503`.

The offset is DETERMINISTIC per autopilot, derived from its id, not random —
that is the whole design. A random delay would have meant sleeping inside the
tick, which breaks the two properties everything else is built on: catch-up
after a missed occurrence, and no-double-run once `lastRunAt` is stamped at or
after the occurrence. Shifting the OCCURRENCE instead keeps it a single
well-defined instant, so both still hold, and tests stay reproducible.

FNV-1a rather than `DefaultHasher`: the standard hasher is explicitly not stable
across Rust releases, and an offset that moved on a toolchain bump would
silently shift every user's schedule. Ids are UUIDs, so the low bits are already
well distributed.

Ten minutes: wide enough to spread a herd across ten tick windows, far enough
under the shortest interval (hourly) that a shifted occurrence can never
overtake the next one, small enough not to surprise someone who picked 09:00.
That upper bound is a `const _: () = assert!(...)` beside the constant rather
than a test — a test comparing two constants is a tautology clippy rejects, and
this makes a bad value unbuildable instead of merely reported.

Tests cover the offset being stable for an id and inside the window, the
occurrence moving by exactly the offset, and the behaviour a user would notice:
between the nominal time and the offset, today's occurrence has NOT been reached,
so the latest is still yesterday's. Plus a full-day minute-by-minute sweep
asserting exactly one transition — one run per day, no double-run, no skip.

Mutation-checked: making the offset always zero fails
`jitter_actually_spreads_a_herd` with "200 autopilots landed in only 1 distinct
minutes".

The AI review flagged `MonitoringPage` as declared-but-not-subscribing. It was
right, and the cause is worse than a stale entry: discovery matched identifiers
against raw source, so PROSE that names a hook counted as a call to it.

A declaration slice runs to the next `export`, which means the doc comment
belonging to the hook BELOW lands inside the preceding hook's body. `use-jobs.ts`
documents `useJob` with "a `useJobEvents()` subscription MUST be mounted

query was dragged into the inventory. That is the same structural fact this repo
already recorded from the other direction: a doc comment sits above its item, so
anything anchored on the item before swallows it.

hook name inside a string is a mention, not a call, and a commented-out
subscription is not one either. It is a scanner rather than a regex on purpose:
`//.*$` would eat the rest of a line after a URL in a string literal, silently
DROPPING a real call — the one failure direction a guard must not have.
Characters are replaced one-for-one with spaces so match offsets stay valid.

`useUpdater` subscribes directly.

comment), a commented-out call, a listener that appears only inside a string, and
that stripping preserves length and line structure.

* fix(autopilot): keep a run in flight visible after navigating away

Reported: created an autopilot, ran it, went to Settings, came back to a card
that looked finished — but the status bar still said a job was running, and
clicking Run answered "a run is already in progress for this autopilot".

Every one of those three signals was correct except the card. The backend held
the run for its full duration (the log shows 301s, dominated by the 300s
semantic re-rank ceiling), the RunGuard refused the second click on purpose,
and the status bar reads the global job registry. Only the card lied, because
its run state is component-local:

* `useAutopilotRun` keeps `runStates`/`stepLogs` in a `useReducer` inside
  `AutopilotPage`, so a route change discards them and the card re-renders
  'idle' — and `inProgress` is deliberately not badged, so nothing else on the
  card contradicts that;
* the same hook owns the step-event subscription, so every step emitted while
  the user was away, terminal `complete` included, was dropped;
* `runAutopilot`'s `onSuccess` invalidation belongs to the unmounted observer,
  so the finished run's found jobs never reached the list either.

* fall back to the persisted `runStatus === 'inProgress'` when this mount has
  no local state for an autopilot, so the card shows 'scraping' and the Run
  button stays disabled;
* let the machine's `idle` accept the mid-run vocabulary, not just the start —
  a card that rejoins mid-run gets `scrape_done`/`complete` with no preceding
  `scrape_start`, and dropping those pinned it back to idle;
* let the terminal states re-arm on `scrape_start`, so the scheduler's next
  occurrence doesn't stream underneath a card frozen on the last outcome;
* invalidate the list when a run ends, which also fixes scheduled runs never
  showing their results until the next navigation;
* stop reverting to 'idle' on `already-running`. That refusal is proof a run is
  in flight, so idle re-armed the button for a click the backend refuses again.

says `inProgress`, and it clears the moment that resolves — including to

backend first flickers a locally-'done' card back to 'scraping' until the

* ci: enforce the rust toolchain pin instead of asking for it in a comment

The pin itself already shipped and is correct: `rust-toolchain.toml` pins
1.97.1, and both `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` uses are pinned to the SHA for that
same version. What was missing is any enforcement.

The two halves cannot reference each other — that action does not read toolchain
files, its `@rev` IS the version selector — so the only thing tying them
together was a comment in three files saying "bump both together". That is the
shape this repo treats as a defect: a stated invariant with nothing checking it.

The failure is quiet, which is what makes it worth a check. Bump the TOML alone
and CI keeps building on the old compiler; bump the action alone and every
developer's machine drifts off what CI validates. Neither goes red on its own —
the pin simply stops meaning anything, which is exactly the state it was created
to end.

`scripts/check-toolchain-pin.mjs` asserts four things: the channel is an exact
three-part version rather than a floating one; every `dtolnay/rust-toolchain`
use under `.github/` carries a trailing `# <version>` comment (an opaque SHA is
unreviewable by construction, so the comment is load-bearing, not decoration);
every one of those declared versions equals the channel; and the Cargo MSRV is
not above the pin, since that pairing cannot compile at all.

It deliberately does NOT verify that the SHA truly is that version — that needs
a network call, and it is not the mistake people make. The realistic error is
updating one place and forgetting the other, which is fully catchable offline.

Wired into the `lint-format` job, which has no path filter and so runs on every
PR — a toolchain drift guard that only fires when Rust files change would miss
the case where someone edits only the workflow. The three comments now name
their enforcer instead of asking nicely.

Guard is mutation-tested five ways against the real repo (bump either half
alone, float the channel back to `stable`, strip a version comment, raise the
MSRV past the pin) — all red, tree restored clean — plus 11 black-box CLI tests
over a fake repo tree, following `check-tech-radar.test.mjs`. One of those
covers removing CI's pin entirely, which would otherwise pass vacuously: with
nothing to compare, nothing disagrees.

* feat(scraping): add freehire as the aggregator's keyless tier

Issue #1002, opened by freehire's maintainer, who disclosed the interest. We
publicly committed to shipping it in the next release.

Implemented from their published openapi.yaml rather than from the PR they
offered. The reason is rights, not code quality: this repo has no CLA, so a
contribution stays under its author's copyright and cannot be relicensed, and
ADR-023 names commercial licensing as a rationale. Reading their PR and
rewriting it would be derivative — the worst of both worlds — so the spec is
the only source used.

What it buys: every other provider needs an API key, so a fresh install gets a
needs-keys skip and zero jobs. freehire answers unauthenticated, so the
aggregator board can return results before the user has configured anything.
It is not a better source than the keyed tiers and is never preferred over
one — it runs LAST, after Adzuna, JSearch and Jooble have each failed to
produce a decisive result, and only a non-empty answer from it short-circuits.
An empty answer from a provider nobody chose is not evidence about the search,
so it must not swallow a configured provider's failure diagnostic.

Two consequences worth calling out rather than burying:

`needs_keys()` is now always false, because a keyless tier is always
"configured". That is the point — the skip existed because a keyless search
could only ever return nothing. The cost, accepted and tested: a keyless user
whose freehire search finds nothing reads "no jobs found" rather than a prompt
to add keys. A keyring READ FAULT is still classified separately, so the one
case the old `false` protected is unaffected.

Failures degrade to Ok(empty), never Err — the only provider with that rule.
Every other one reports its failure because a stored key means the user asked
for it specifically. Nobody opted into this one, so surfacing its outage would
turn a third party's downtime into an error banner on a search the user never
aimed at them. There is no SLA and no rate-limit header of any kind (verified:
no X-RateLimit-*, no Retry-After), so it is treated as always-possibly-absent.

Uses the documented /agent/jobs/search with `q` and
`description_format=markdown` — NOT the undocumented /jobs/search taking
`query`, which is what the issue described and what a first pass reached for;
building from the published spec is the whole basis for implementing this
ourselves. Markdown up front is also what keeps scoring from needing a
per-result detail fetch.

A guessed country is deliberately not sent as a filter: the aggregator defaults
`country` to "de" when the caller supplied none, and pinning a keyless tier to
that guess would reproduce the guessed-market bug already fixed for Adzuna.
`location` is unused because the documented search has no city parameter at
all, and folding a city into the full-text `q` would drop every posting that
does not spell its city out, remote ones included.

Egress: freehire.me is in the inventory with a public_name, which made the
landing drift guard fail until the privacy page, README and SECURITY named it.
That guard shipped two PRs ago for exactly this, and this is the first new
egress since — it worked.

baseline, red with the feature deleted, restored. The one claim that did not
survive checking is recorded in the test rather than quietly dropped — the

* feat(pipeline): revert a repair round that introduces cross-section incoherence

An audit found the codebase's only two cross-section coherence checks -
duplicate.bullet and consistency.skill_not_demonstrated - are computed and then
thrown away. repair acts on Criticals only, humanize on voice.* only. Measured
consequences, both accepted and persisted: a round that doubled the whole
document produced 5 duplicate.bullet warnings at duplicateRatio 1.00 and
shipped; a round that deleted an employment entry produced 4
skill_not_demonstrated warnings and shipped.

The naive fix is to revert when those warnings are present, and it is wrong.
The same audit measured them false-positiving under per-section generation:
rewording two Experience bullets to drop the exact tokens - the ordinary
outcome of a rewrite that cannot see the Skills section - raises four warnings
on a truthful document. An absolute threshold would revert good rounds and
would need calibrating against noise.

So the term is a DELTA, not a count. The question is not whether the document
carries cross-section warnings but whether THIS ROUND introduced any that were
not there before. Four before and four after reverts nothing; four before and
nine after reverts. That needs no threshold, is immune to the measured baseline
false positives, and matches the before/after shape round_is_worse already uses
for its newly-introduced-absence term.

Per code rather than summed, so a round that fixes two duplicate.bullet
warnings while introducing two skill_not_demonstrated ones cannot hide a
regression behind an unrelated improvement - a case a summed total reads as
flat, and which the mutation check confirmed only the per-code form catches.

Also closes two advisories from the security review of da4926f0: the anchor is
trimmed once at its source, so repair_system's gate and repair_user's own
emptiness test can no longer disagree about whether a document_context block
exists; and the context rule now says to match the language and tense OBSERVED
there, naming it a writing sample rather than asking the model to conform to
untrusted content.

* fix: anchor the pipeline elapsed timer on the run's own start time

GeneratingPanel reset its elapsed clock to 0:00 on every remount because it

per-step start too, but that requires walking a persisted event log across

so a simple, always-correct per-run number wins. The caption's copy changes
accordingly (pipeline.step.elapsedTotal, en+de) since it now reads total run
time rather than time-in-this-step.

safe to re-run every boot since it is lookup-only and can never create
an Application.

Split the backfill + its marker out of applications/mod.rs into
migrations.rs (same store, same pattern as reminders.rs/contact.rs) to
stay under the R8 LOC cap, and allowlist that file for R3's rusqlite
confinement rule, mirroring the existing per-domain-store entries.

* test(applications): close two mutation-surviving gaps in the backfill link tests

Every existing link_orphaned_generations test seeds the orphan row with
an already-normalized job_url, so deleting the internal
normalize_job_url call inside link_orphaned_generations still leaves
every one of them green. Add a test that seeds the RAW url a genuine
pre-fix row would carry.

Also add a test at exactly APPLICATIONS_FEATURE_EPOCH_MS: every
existing epoch-guard test uses a value safely past the boundary, so
`>` silently passes where `>=` is required. This pins the inclusive
boundary directly.

* fix: round a per-call timeout up to whole seconds, never truncate to 0s

timeout_message and timeout_failure_data both divided milliseconds by
1000, truncating down. A sub-second per-call timeout -- reachable once
effort scales the deadline down far enough -- rendered "within 0s" and
shipped seconds: 0 to the renderer's timeout banner.

Extract a shared round_up_seconds (div_ceil(1000).max(1)) so the
English message and the structured event payload always agree on the
same non-zero rounded value. Update the two pinned tests for the
rounding change (300_021ms now reports 301s, not 300s -- ceiling, not
truncation) and add a dedicated sub-second regression test where
truncation and ceiling diverge to 0 vs 1.

* fix: match the save verdict exhaustively instead of unreachable!()

The Ok(()) if refused arm re-derived the refusal reason by
re-destructuring verdict with a let-else unreachable!() fallback,
trusting it to stay in sync with the separately-computed refused bool.
A future edit to one without the other would panic inside the spawned
run task, leaving the job with no terminal event.

Nest a single exhaustive match on the verdict inside the Ok(()) arm
instead, so a new verdict variant is a compile error here, never a
runtime panic on a fallible path.

* fix(applications): correct the architecture-allowlist claim about the backfill's connection

The allowlist comment said applications/migrations.rs's persistence "lives
entirely inside the applications domain store, on the SAME connection" -
false: backfill_from_generations (and link_orphaned_generations) open a
second connection onto the sibling ai_generations.db to read and link its
rows. Reword to match the code.

* fix(applications): stop leaking a path through the boot-time backfill warn logs

Both open()-time warn! calls interpolated the AppError's Display directly.
rusqlite::Error::InvalidPath embeds the offending filesystem path in its
Display text, which AppError::from preserves, so a failed
crate::db::open(&gen_path) could log an absolute path (repo path-privacy
rule, and the same thing tests::architecture::r15_no_display_in_log_macros
already guards against generally). Log AppError::code() instead - a fixed,
path-free category string, exactly what it exists for.

* fix(applications): stop legacy_backfill_done swallowing a real read error into false

Every query_row error, not just QueryReturnedNoRows, was mapped to false via
is_ok() - a transient SQLite failure looked identical to "not done yet" and
re-ran the one-shot legacy scan, which recreates a deliberately-deleted
Application (the exact bug the marker exists to prevent), reachable through
a different door. Return AppResult<bool> and use .optional()? so only
QueryReturnedNoRows reads as "not done"; every other error now propagates
through backfill_from_generations's existing ? into ApplicationStore::
open's non-fatal warn-log path.

* fix(applications): log dropped legacy generation rows instead of silently discarding them

.filter_map(|r| r.ok()) discarded any row whose column mapping failed, then
the one-shot marker got set as if every row had been processed - so a
dropped row is never retried. Count the drops and log them at warn once the
scan finishes; the message is a bare count only, never the row's id/company/
url (path-free, content-free per ADR-027), since the marker this scan feeds
is one-shot and this is the only signal the loss is ever diagnosable from.

* fix(applications): relink stranded legacy generations after a restore, not just at boot

data_import replaces aiGenerations wholesale via AiGenerationStore::import,
but never touched the legacy-backfill marker. Restoring a pre-
ApplicationStore-era backup (one whose bundle has no "applications" section)
left its generations with application_id = NULL forever: the marker is
already set from the very first boot, long before any later restore, so
ApplicationStore::open's one-shot scan never even sees them again.

Extract the scan body into scan_legacy_generations (shared, marker-free) and
add ApplicationStore::relink_legacy_generations_after_restore, called from
data_import only when the bundle replaced aiGenerations but carries no
"applications" section - i.e. verifiably predates ApplicationStore, so none
of its rows can be a deliberately AiGenerationStore::detach_application-ed
row (that capability did not exist yet when such a bundle was exported).
A modern bundle that DOES carry "applications" is left alone: it already
restores self-consistent application_id links via the two imports, and CAN
legitimately carry a deliberately-detached row that re-scanning would
resurrect - the exact bug the one-shot marker exists to prevent.

* test(applications): cover the marker-set-last guarantee on a partial backfill failure

Only the success path was tested. Poison one row's link-back write with a
SQLite trigger so backfill_from_generations fails strictly between the
first row's committed Application and the second row's write, then assert
the one-shot marker stays unset and a later boot retries and finishes the
row it never reached, without spawning a duplicate Application for the row
whose creation already succeeded before its own write failed.

* fix(data): resolve the restore relink data dir like setup and test its gate

Two review findings on the restore-specific relink, both in one file.

The relink resolved its directory with a bare `app.path().app_data_dir()` and
skipped entirely when that failed. Setup resolves through
`resolve_and_export_data_dir`, which falls back to `platform::config::data_dir()`
— so on a host where the bare call errors, every store still opened through the
fallback and the one-shot boot marker got set, while the relink (the only thing
that can still repair those rows) silently did not run. The marker turns a
skipped repair into a permanent one, so the two resolutions must not differ.

The gate `aiGenerations present && applications absent` is the whole boundary
that stops a modern full backup from resurrecting a deliberately-detached row,
and nothing tested it. Lifted into a pure `is_legacy_generations_only_bundle`
and tested across all four combinations, exactly one of which may return true.
Chosen over a source-pin test: a pin asserts text exists in a file, not that
the decision is right, and goes stale silently when the code is reshaped.

Mutation-tested all three ways the condition can be weakened — `&&` to `||`,
and dropping either operand — each reddens the four-combination test.
